title: Counterexample-guided repair of a finite-sum inference
objective: Map the boundary between true and false versions of the following informal inference: local pairwise lower constraints on a finite family of real numbers force a useful global lower bound on their total sum. Generate several precise candidate formulations, use small finite countermodels to eliminate overgeneralizations, identify assumptions that are sufficient without being vacuous, and kernel-check at least one corrected theorem in Lean 4.
success_definition: The program should not merely prove a supplied theorem. It must explore multiple formalizations, expose at least one false generalization, explain why it fails, and converge to a corrected statement whose assumptions and scope are explicit.
deliverables: A hypothesis map containing false and corrected formulations across at least two finite dimensions.
Executable counterexample searches for rejected formulations.
A Lean 4 plus Mathlib proof of at least one nontrivial corrected theorem.
A dependency explanation showing which assumptions do real logical work.
resources: Lean 4 environment resolved through ASTRA_LOCAL_LEAN4_ROOT or the configured ASTRUM oracle
linear_control_directions: Formalize one pairwise-constraint statement for three real variables.
Search bounded rational assignments for a counterexample.
Repeat the search for four real variables.
Add nonnegativity assumptions and retest the statement.
Derive a summed inequality from all pairwise constraints.
Identify a concise sufficient assumption set.
Encode the corrected finite-dimensional statement in Lean 4.
Kernel-check the theorem and summarize the assumption boundary.

expert_anchors.goal_advancement: Coverage and clarity of the true/false boundary for the family of local-to-global inferences.
expert_anchors.hypothesis_quality: Precision, falsifiability, and nontriviality of the alternative formulations and assumption sets.
expert_anchors.research_depth: Whether countermodels drive principled theorem repair and generalization rather than disconnected attempts.
expert_anchors.evidence_quality: Correct use of exact countermodels, domain declarations, Lean kernel checking, and separation of testing from proof.
expert_anchors.self_correction: Recognition of failed generalizations and disciplined repair without silently changing the target.
expert_anchors.cross_perspective_uptake: Whether a minority proposal supplies a countermodel, missing assumption, proof lemma, or alternate formalization used later.
expert_anchors.novelty_utility: Value of the resulting assumption map as a reusable logical pattern or formalization example.
expert_anchors.artifact_reproducibility: Lean source, toolchain metadata, counterexample code, exact witnesses, and unambiguous theorem statements.
